Row: One active SS3 input row, its original line number and comment retained for provenance; comments do not override parsed numeric settings.
Reader: Strict row-oriented reader for the supplied SS3 version, retaining source lines and rejecting unsupported layouts or trailing rows.
Reader.__init__: Read a UTF-8 SS3 file, verify its version prefix and retain active token rows with original source locations.
Reader.take: Consume one active row and optionally require an exact token count; fail with a source location on EOF or mismatch.
Reader.numbers: Consume one numeric row and reject malformed or nonfinite values with the original file/line context.
Reader.scalar: Consume a row containing exactly one finite numeric value.
Reader.integer: Consume one scalar and require it to represent an exact integer.
Reader.expect: Require the next row to equal a supported setting exactly instead of silently accepting another SS3 configuration.
Reader.table: Read rows of a fixed-width source table until the supported sentinel is encountered.
Reader.finish: Require the source terminator and reject additional active rows after the supported configuration.
ints: Convert numeric values to integers only when every value is exactly integral.
parameter: Read one control parameter record, validate its width, finite bounds and initialization, and retain its canonical name and source location.
parse_data: Parse the supported swordfish data layout, including original catches, indices, included/excluded length samples and calendar metadata.
validate_data: Check observation years, fleets, positive errors/sample sizes, finite counts and duplicate sample keys before generating C++ data.
parse_control: Parse supported biological, selectivity, recruitment, catchability, hybrid-F and likelihood settings; reject unimplemented flags/layouts.
load_inputs: Read and validate the paired data/control files, retaining hashes and explicit control/report distinctions for preparation.
save_if_changed: Write a generated artifact only when content differs, preserving header timestamps to avoid unnecessary recompilation.
cpp: Serialize supported scalar, string and nested-list input values as C++ initializer expressions.
generate_header: Generate a C++ InputData factory from parsed original observations and controls, with optional observation subsets for audits.
generate_header.assign: Append one named field assignment with a typed serialized initializer to the generated C++ factory.
report_table: Locate a version-specific rectangular Report.sso section and return its header and token rows for comparison fixtures.
generate_replay: Export report-only historical population/biology comparison targets; these fixtures are not drivers of the independent model calculation.
read_lines: Read source text into lines using the supplied report encoding conventions.
section: Find an exact SS3 section label and return its bounded source lines; reject missing sections.
extract: Extract a checked header and pattern-matched rows from one version-specific report section.
write_csv: Write a header and extracted rows to a reference CSV while preserving column order.
scripts/prepare_biology.py::prepare: Generate biological input/parameter mappings and report fixtures, validating canonical parameter order and reporting the fixed male-growth discrepancy.
scripts/prepare_population.py::prepare: Generate original-catch population inputs, early/main fitted deviation mappings and initialization targets from the supplied report.
scripts/prepare_likelihood.py::prepare: Validate the supported starter/forecast likelihood settings and generate named likelihood/index/length comparison targets.
active: Return nonempty source lines after removing comments to check supported starter and forecast settings.
scripts/compare_projections.py::read: Read a named projection CSV from the example build output folder.
scripts/check_projection_uncertainty.py:: Read a CSV with column labels into dictionaries for independent uncertainty artifact validation.
prepare.case: Append one labeled biological fixture row with year, timing, sex, fleet, age, bin and reference value.
